questions.solution_html:
• AI refers to machines or systems that simulate human intelligence.
  • Types
  •  Narrow AI (specific tasks) EG: Siri, Alexa, chatgpt
  •  General AI (human-level intelligence) eg: Hypothetical future AI
  •  Super AI (beyond human intelligence) eg: theoretical concept

questions.question: Differentiate between threats, vulnerabilities, and risks with examples.
questions.solution_html:
•  Threats: A potential danger or harmful event that could exploit a weakness in a
  • system. (e.g., Malware attacks (viruses, ransomware), Phishing emails, Unauthorized
  • access, etc.)
  •  Vulnerability: A weakness or flaw in software, hardware, network, or human
  • processes that can be exploited by a threat. (e.g., Outdated software, Weak passwords
  • Unpatched operating system, Unsecured Wi-Fi)
  •  Risk: potential damage from a threat exploiting a vulnerability (e.g., Data loss due to
  • unpatched systems attacked by malware, financial loss from phishing scam)
questions.final_answer: unpatched systems attacked by malware, financial loss from phishing scam)
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain the different service models with examples.
questions.solution_html:
• SaaS (Software as a Service): ready-to-use applications (e.g., Gmail, Office 365)
  • PaaS (Platform as a Service): for app development (e.g., Google App Engine)
  • IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service): virtual hardware resources (e.g., AWS EC2)
  • Explanation of each in detail. ((7.5 marks))
  • Architecture diagram ((2.5 marks))

questions.question: Discuss the architecture and components of a robot with a neat / diagram.
questions.solution_html:
• Main Components
  • Sensors: detect environment
  • Actuators: control motion
  • Controller: brain of robot
  • Power Supply
  • End Effector: tool performing task ((8 marks))
  • Architecture Diagram: Input (Sensors) → Processor → Output (Actuators) ((2 marks))
